caution: A failure to reproduce is not a finding that the paper is wrong. It may be a failure of the attempt.

attempts.label: DANDI:000981
attempts.paper_title: Whole-brain chemosensory responses of both C. elegans sexes

inputs.what: Chemical connectomes of the hermaphrodite (White et al. 1986 as annotated by Cook et al.) and the male, as synapse counts (Supplementary Information 3, 41586_2019_1352_MOESM6_ESM.xlsx) and as EM serial sections (Supplementary Information 5, 41586_2019_1352_MOESM9_ESM.xlsx), used by the connectome claims.
Synapse count matrices of datasets 7 and 8 (41586_2021_3778_MOESM4_ESM.xlsx), used by the connectome claims.

Method details the claims file cites from the paper's code (onset frames of config.py, the response windows and baseline of compile_all_traces.ipynb, the code's extra exclusion filters of Fig2&3_prepare_data.ipynb, the class collapsing of Fig5.ipynb, the band-pass filter and the stimulus series of compile_all_traces.ipynb and Fig4_prepare_data.ipynb). Parameters only; no data. The code's four band-pass functions are copied into the notebook to check the helper on a toy trace.

attempts.entry_title: Whole-brain chemosensory responses of both C. elegans sexes (Seyedolmohadesin et al. 2026)
attempts.summary: Most of the paper's main findings held up in this data: nearly all head neuron classes respond to the cues, most respond differently in the two sexes, sensory neurons are the most dimorphic layer, functional connectivity is similar between the sexes (R2 = 0.806), and functional dimorphism does not track synaptic dimorphism. Three finer findings did not hold: fewer sensory classes than stated were both dimorphic and monomorphic, AWA did not respond to copper, and ASER's low-salt dimorphism fell just short (p = 0.055). Whether the most functionally dimorphic pairs lack synapses could not be tested, as it depends on a connectome form the paper does not name. Tail neurons were untestable: the dataset holds only head traces.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Seyedolmohadesin et al. (2026) on dandiset 000981, which holds whole-head calcium imaging of 22 hermaphrodites and 25 males during repeated presentation of ten chemosensory stimuli. It tests which neuron classes respond and which respond differently in the two sexes, examples of single classes, the dependence on motor state, and the functional connectivity of the two sexes. The connectome comparisons need published connectomes and the behavioural assays are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Seyedolmohadesin et al. (2026) from dandiset 000981

outcomes.statement: Whole-head activity of 196 sex-shared and 6 male-specific neurons was studied in 22 hermaphrodites and 25 males.
outcomes.source: Results, Most sensory neurons in the head exhibit sexually dimorphic responses, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: We studied the activity of 196 sex-shared neurons ... in the heads of 22 hermaphrodites and 25 males
outcomes.notes: The subject descriptions give 22 hermaphrodites and 25 males, and the subject ids agree. Files 20220403-h3 and 20220403-m3 hold the same trace table, which is h3's traces followed by m3's; split in two, every animal has traces of its own. The traces cover 189 distinct sex-shared neuron names (the paper says 196 sex-shared neurons were studied) and the 6 male-specific neurons.
deviations: The shared table of 20220403-h3 and 20220403-m3 is split at the row where its first label recurs; the first block (187 traces) is taken as h3's and the second (195 traces, with the male-specific neurons) as m3's, because their responses match the other animals' when read with h3's and m3's stimulus orders respectively (mean r 0.58 and 0.54, against 0.32 and 0.31 with the other order).

outcomes.statement: Of the 89 head neuron classes, 84 (94%) responded to at least one stimulus in at least one sex.
outcomes.source: Results, Most sensory neurons in the head exhibit sexually dimorphic responses, paragraph 9; Figure 5B
outcomes.quote: Of the 89 neuron classes in the head, 84 were responsive (94%)
outcomes.notes: 86 of 89 canonical classes are responsive under exclusion (a) and 85 under (b), at p <= 0.05 and at p < 0.05 alike (not responsive AVD, I4 and RMG, and AQR under (b)). Each subclass has 32 tests (8 cues, 2 windows, 2 sexes), and 22.1% of all tests are significant, so the count is near its ceiling; this is the paper's test as written. The paper states no chance level. With 32 uncorrected tests per class, a class with no effect would be called responsive with probability up to 1 - 0.95^32 = 0.81 if the tests were independent, so about 72 of 89 classes could be expected by chance and the count is weakly diagnostic.
deviations: The code's identification-confidence filter (conf == 1) cannot be applied; the dandiset has no confidence values. Its time ranges to ignore are already blank in the traces; its ganglia to ignore per recording cannot be checked.
Onset frames are the code's (config.py ON_stim), as the claims file says; the dandiset's annotations lie 1 to 3 frames later.

outcomes.statement: Of the 89 head neuron classes, 80 (90%) responded dimorphically to at least one stimulus.
outcomes.source: Results, Most sensory neurons in the head exhibit sexually dimorphic responses, paragraph 9; Figure 5B
outcomes.quote: and 80 classes (90%) were sexually dimorphic
outcomes.notes: Dimorphic and responsive (reading a, the code's) 83 classes under exclusion (a) and 82 under (b); dimorphic alone (reading b) 86 and 85. All four are within 80 plus or minus 8. 20.9% of the 1760 subclass-cue-window sex tests have p <= 0.05, 7.6% after Benjamini-Hochberg over all of them.

outcomes.statement: Responsive and dimorphic classes per layer are 23 and 22 of 24 sensory, 34 and 33 of 36 inter, 14 and 13 of 15 motor, and 13 and 12 of 14 pharyngeal classes.
outcomes.source: Results, Most sensory neurons in the head exhibit sexually dimorphic responses, paragraph 9; Figure 5B
outcomes.quote: Of the 24 sensory neuron classes, 23 classes (96%) were responsive, and 22 classes (92%) were dimorphic. Of the 36 interneuron classes, 34 classes (94%) were responsive, and 33 classes (92%) were dimorphic. Of the 15 motor neuron classes, 14 classes (93%) were responsive, and 13 classes (87%) were dimorphic. Of the 14 pharyngeal neuron classes, 13 classes (93%) were responsive, and 12 classes (86%) were dimorphic
outcomes.notes: With the layers of Figure 3A and dimorphism reading (a), dimorphic and responsive, all eight counts are within tolerance under both exclusion readings. Exclusion (a), sensory 24 responsive and 24 dimorphic, inter 35 and 34, motor 14 and 14, pharyngeal 13 and 11; exclusion (b), 23 and 22, 35 and 34, 14 and 14, 13 and 12. Reading (b), dimorphic alone, has seven of eight within tolerance (motor dimorphic 15). With the assignment the first version assumed (IL1 motor, URB sensory, RMG inter), shown as a variant, seven of eight hold under every combination (motor 15 and 15). The name colours of Figures 3A (onset) and 3B (offset), read together, give exactly the paper's Figure 5B counts with these layers (responsive 23, 34, 14, 13; dimorphic 22, 33, 13, 12), which confirms the assignment, and no gray name is red, as in reading (a). Subclass by subclass this analysis gives the figure's colour for 101 of 110 subclasses under exclusion (a) and 105 under (b). The per-stimulus counts of Data S4 remain unchecked.
deviations: The layer of each canonical class is read from the column groups of Figure 3A (headings Sensory, Interneuron, Motor and Pharyngeal over the subclass labels), as the claims file's CLASSES leaves it OPEN and the code's neuron_classes.json is not public. Collapsed to canonical classes it gives the paper's totals (24, 36, 15, 14), with IL1 sensory, URB an interneuron and RMG a motor neuron; it is listed in the notebook's data check and in chemo.LAYER_CLASSES.

outcomes.statement: For every stimulus at least one neuron class responds dimorphically and at least one monomorphically.
outcomes.source: Results, Most sensory neurons in the head exhibit sexually dimorphic responses, paragraph 5; Figure 3A and 3B; Figure 5B
outcomes.quote: For each stimulus tested, we observed at least one neuron class respond in a sexually dimorphic manner, and one class respond in a monomorphic manner
outcomes.notes: Under both exclusion readings each of the 8 cues has dimorphic canonical classes (22 to 54) and monomorphic ones (14 to 34). A canonical class is dimorphic to a cue when any subclass is, and monomorphic when it is responsive to the cue and no subclass is dimorphic to it.
deviations: The criterion does not say whether classes are subclasses or canonical classes; canonical classes are used, as Figure 5B counts them (claims file, criterion).

outcomes.statement: Nearly every sensory neuron class responds dimorphically to at least one stimulus and monomorphically to at least one other.
outcomes.source: Discussion, paragraph 1; Figures 3 and 5A
outcomes.quote: nearly every sensory neuron responds in a sexually dimorphic manner to at least one stimulus while responding monomorphically to at least one other stimulus
outcomes.notes: 21 of 24 sensory classes are dimorphic to one cue and monomorphic to another under exclusion (a) (ASJ, FLP and OLL have no monomorphic cue) and 20 of 24 under (b) (AQR, IL2, OLL and URX), against at least 22. All are dimorphic to at least one cue except IL2 under (b). The sensory classes are those of Figure 3A; the threshold of 22 is the claims file's reading of "nearly every". The assignment the first version assumed gives the same counts.

outcomes.statement: Dimorphic and monomorphic responses are less present in interneurons than in sensory neurons, and less still in motor neurons.
outcomes.source: Summary; Figures 3A, 3B and 5B
outcomes.quote: This dimorphic and monomorphic activity was present to a lesser extent in downstream interneurons and even less so in motoneurons
outcomes.notes: With the layers of Figure 3A, under reading (c) the share of subclass-cue-window cells that are dimorphic is 0.260 in sensory, 0.197 in inter and 0.180 in motor subclasses under exclusion (a), and 0.254, 0.198 and 0.150 under (b); under reading (b), the share of class-cue combinations that are responsive, 0.688, 0.566 and 0.517 (a) and 0.677, 0.587 and 0.475 (b). Reading (a), class-cue combinations dimorphic, does not order them (sensory 0.495, inter 0.368, motor 0.408). The criterion asks for one reading. With the assignment the first version assumed, reading (c) holds under both exclusions and reading (b) under exclusion (b) only.

outcomes.statement: At the onset of osmotic stress ASER and ASH respond monomorphically while AWA and AWB respond dimorphically.
outcomes.source: Results, Most sensory neurons in the head exhibit sexually dimorphic responses, paragraph 5; Figures 2B and 3A
outcomes.quote: in response to the onset of osmotic stress, the gustatory neuron ASER and the nociceptive neuron ASH ... show monomorphic responses, whereas olfactory neurons AWA and AWB ... show dimorphic responses
outcomes.notes: At sorbitol onset, exclusion (a), AWA p = 4.2e-11 (normalized difference 0.66) and AWB p = 7.1e-07 (0.64) are dimorphic; ASER p = 0.45 and ASH p = 0.80 are not, and both respond to sorbitol in each sex (control comparison p 3.7e-06 or below). The same under exclusion (b), with control comparison p 4.5e-06 or below.

outcomes.statement: AWA's response to osmotic stress is dimorphic and BAG's response to high odor is monomorphic.
outcomes.source: Figure 2B legend
outcomes.quote: exemplifying sexually dimorphic (e.g., AWA responding to osmotic stress) and monomorphic neural activity (e.g., BAG responding to high odor)
outcomes.notes: Under all three readings and both exclusion readings. AWA sorbitol onset p = 4.2e-11, offset p = 0.00027; BAG high odor onset p = 0.78, offset p = 0.38 (normalized differences 0.01 and 0.08), responsive in both sexes (control comparison p 0.00029 or below).

outcomes.statement: ASH responds monomorphically to osmotic and toxic stress but dimorphically to high salt.
outcomes.source: Results, Most sensory neurons in the head exhibit sexually dimorphic responses, paragraph 5; Figures 2B and 3A
outcomes.quote: the ASH neuron's response to osmotic and toxic stress is monomorphic, but its response to high salt is dimorphic
outcomes.notes: At onset, ASH high salt hermaphrodites 1.66 and males 0.27, p = 8e-13; sorbitol p = 0.80 and CuSO4 p = 0.13, both responsive in each sex. Same under exclusion (b) (9.8e-14, 0.98, 0.18).

outcomes.statement: ASER responds dimorphically to low salt but monomorphically to high salt.
outcomes.source: Results, Most sensory neurons in the head exhibit sexually dimorphic responses, paragraph 5; Figures 2B and 3A
outcomes.quote: the ASER neuron's response to a low concentration of salt is dimorphic, but its response to a higher concentration of salt is monomorphic
outcomes.notes: At onset ASER's low-salt response is hermaphrodites -0.029 and males -0.102 (normalized difference 0.31), p = 0.055 under exclusion (a) and 0.059 under (b), just above the threshold. Its high-salt response does not differ between sexes (p = 0.89) but is not responsive in either sex (control comparison p = 0.72 and 0.33), so it is not monomorphic in the sense of Figures 3 and 5 either. About 60 responses per sex enter (ASER is one neuron).

outcomes.statement: Pharyngeal interneuron I2 responds dimorphically to pheromone, osmotic stress and salt.
outcomes.source: Results, Most sensory neurons in the head exhibit sexually dimorphic responses, paragraph 7; Figure 2E
outcomes.quote: pharyngeal interneuron I2 exhibited sexually dimorphic responses to pheromone, osmotic stress, and salt
outcomes.notes: Exclusion (a), I2 pheromone onset p = 4.4e-10 and offset p = 0.00014; sorbitol onset p = 0.034; high salt onset p = 0.015; low salt p 0.47 or more. Exclusion (b) gives 0.022 for sorbitol and 0.010 for high salt. Onset only, all three hold; offset only, pheromone alone; the salt that holds is the high one.

outcomes.statement: The pharyngeal (enteric) neurons respond dimorphically to food, salt and pheromone.
outcomes.source: Discussion, paragraph 4; Figure 2E
outcomes.quote: the enteric nervous system of the worm responds to food, salt, and (most strikingly) pheromone in a sexually dimorphic manner
outcomes.notes: Under both exclusion readings pharyngeal subclasses are dimorphic to food (I4, M2, M5), to pheromone (I2, I3, I4, I5, M2, M4, MC, NSM), to low salt (four or five) and to high salt (six).
deviations: Pharyngeal classes from Figure 3A; they are also the dandiset's own "pharyngeal" neuron group.

outcomes.statement: Olfactory neurons AWA and AWB also respond to osmotic and toxic stress.
outcomes.source: Results, Most sensory neurons in the head exhibit sexually dimorphic responses, paragraph 7; Figure 2B
outcomes.quote: in addition to responding to odors, olfactory neurons AWA and AWB also responded to nociceptive stimuli, including osmotic and toxic stress
outcomes.notes: AWB responds to sorbitol and CuSO4 in both sexes (p 0.0046 or below at onset). AWA responds to sorbitol in hermaphrodites (onset p = 3.5e-11, offset p = 0.00019) but not in males, and to CuSO4 in neither sex nor window (smallest p 0.077 under exclusion (a), 0.085 under (b)). Three of the four class-cue pairs hold. The criterion requires all four and names no partial outcome, so the outcome is not reproduced (changed from partially reproduced after round 1).

outcomes.statement: ADF responds to food in hermaphrodites but to pheromone in males, and pharyngeal neuron M2 shows a similar switch between food and pheromone.
outcomes.source: Results, Most sensory neurons in the head exhibit sexually dimorphic responses, paragraph 7; Figures 2B and 2E
outcomes.quote: ADF responds to food in hermaphrodites, but in males it responds to pheromones ... More surprising was a similar dimorphic switch in the M2 pharyngeal neuron, also to food and pheromone
outcomes.notes: ADF meets reading (b) under both exclusion readings, food onset 3.93 in hermaphrodites against 0.76 in males and pheromone onset 5.96 in males against 0.07, both dimorphic (p below 1e-4); reading (a) fails as males also respond to food (onset p below 1e-4 against control). M2 meets reading (b) under both (food onset 0.31 against 0.01, pheromone onset 0.21 in males against -0.01 and -0.02, p below 1e-4), and reading (a) under exclusion (b), where its hermaphrodite pheromone response has p = 0.051.

outcomes.statement: The male-specific head neuron classes CEM and MCM were predominantly unresponsive to the stimuli.
outcomes.source: Results, Most sensory neurons in the head exhibit sexually dimorphic responses, paragraph 2; Figure S2D (the text cites S2C; the legend of S2D shows the male-specific neurons)
outcomes.quote: The male-specific head neuron classes (sensory neuron CEM and interneuron MCM) were predominantly unresponsive to stimuli
outcomes.notes: Of 16 tests each in males, CEMD 0 significant, CEMV 2 (3 under exclusion (b)), MCM 1. Over the sex-shared subclasses 22.3% of male tests are significant, so these classes are below the general rate.

outcomes.statement: Tail neurons did not appear to respond to cues presented to the head.
outcomes.source: Results, Broad chemosensory stimulation activates the whole brain of both sexes, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: tail neurons did not appear to be responsive to cues presented to the head
outcomes.notes: The trace tables hold head neurons only. The NeuroPAL segmentations identify tail neurons (PHA, PHB, PLM, PVQ, DVA and others), but none has a trace, and the paper says tail neurons were recorded. A listing of every group and dataset of two files (data check) shows no trace table other than ActivityTraces. The tracked ROIs (TrackedNeuronROIs) of 20220327-h2 include 31 tail neurons with one ROI per volume. Read in full in all 47 files, 99.75% of the 44,677,593 tracked ROIs have coordinates (0, 0, 0), none has a coordinate above 2, and all 284,479 ROIs of tail neurons (11 files) are zero, so their traces cannot be re-extracted from the raw volumes at the tracked positions; doing so would mean tracking them again. No other public source of these traces is named in the paper.

outcomes.statement: Neurons within the same class usually have equivalent activity, with left and right neurons more correlated with each other than with neurons of other classes.
outcomes.source: Results, Most sensory neurons in the head exhibit sexually dimorphic responses, paragraph 3; Figure S2F
outcomes.quote: Neurons within the same class usually exhibit equivalent neural-activity traces
outcomes.notes: With band-passed traces the mean left-right r exceeds the mean r with other classes for 77 of 79 bilateral subclasses in hermaphrodites and 80 of 82 in males (mean 0.44 against 0.04 and 0.05); with raw traces for 72 of 79 and 73 of 82. Per animal, a median 85% of bilateral subclasses meet it. MC is the main exception.

outcomes.statement: Restricting the test to the first cycle or to per-animal averages makes specific neuron-stimulus pairs less clearly dimorphic but leaves the pattern of dimorphic neuron classes largely unchanged.
outcomes.source: Results, Most sensory neurons in the head exhibit sexually dimorphic responses, paragraph 10; Figure S3A to S3E
outcomes.quote: Overall, while specific odor-neuron pairs are not as clearly dimorphic in these more conservative analyses, the pattern of neurons that we find to respond dimorphically is largely unaffected
outcomes.notes: Of the 103 subclasses dimorphic under representation 1 (exclusion (a)), 87 (84%) remain under representation 2, 94 (91%) under representation 3 and 80 (78%) under all three; exclusion (b) 85%, 96% and 83%. Dimorphic subclass-cue-window pairs drop from 368 to 262 and 254 (355 to 256 and 255). Both readings hold.

outcomes.statement: Response amplitude does not depend on the position of the stimulus in the presentation order.
outcomes.source: Results, Most sensory neurons in the head exhibit sexually dimorphic responses, paragraph 10; Figure S2E
outcomes.quote: We also verified that there was no dependence on response amplitude as a function of stimulus order
outcomes.notes: All stimuli combined, cycle 1 onset responses. Under exclusion (b) no reading finds a dependence (regression slope p = 0.119, per-animal regression p = 0.431, ANOVA p = 0.056), which gives reproduced. Under exclusion (a) the regressions find none (p = 0.063 and 0.335) and the ANOVA finds one (p = 0.034), which by the criterion gives blocked. The mean response by position ranges from 0.036 to 0.063 with no trend. The claims file blocks a claim when its exclusion readings give different outcomes (opening comment, EXCLUSION and READINGS). Per stimulus, the ANOVA has p below 0.05 for food, osmotic, low odor, low salt and buffer under both exclusions; the only slope below 0.05 is high salt under exclusion (a) (p = 0.011). The question of which test and which neurons Figure S2E uses is for the paper's authors (findings).

outcomes.statement: Motor-state-dependent sexual dimorphism is more prominent in interneurons than in sensory or motor neurons.
outcomes.source: Results, Most sensory neurons in the head exhibit sexually dimorphic responses, paragraph 11; Figure S3F and S3G
outcomes.quote: These state-dependent responses were more prominent in interneurons than in sensory or motor neurons
outcomes.notes: Of the 48 combinations of the open motor-state details (AVA trace, change measure, fit divided or subtracted, fit to the whole trace or to its baseline) and the two exclusion readings, the interneurons have the highest share of state-dependent dimorphic cells in 36 at q < 0.05 and in 44 at p < 0.05. Ten of the 12 exceptions at q < 0.05 use the fit to the baseline, under which 0 to 9 of the 640 interneuron cells reach q < 0.05; the other two are AVAR alone, divided by the fit to the whole trace, with (max - min) / mean, under each exclusion reading. Under the main reading (mean of AVAL and AVAR, divided by the whole-trace fit, (max - min) / mean, exclusion a), 0 of 496 sensory, 4 of 640 inter and 0 of 400 motor cells have q < 0.05, and 40, 75 and 41 have p < 0.05 (8.1%, 11.7% and 10.3%). No combination has more than 13 interneuron cells at q < 0.05. The claims file blocks the claim when the motor-state readings disagree (opening comment, READINGS). The layers of Figure 3A and the earlier assumed ones give the same counts of combinations. The open details are a question for the paper's authors (findings).
deviations: The exponential a * exp(-k t) + c is fitted by least squares either to the whole AVA trace or to its baseline, the 10th percentile of each 100-frame bin (Methods, "estimating the baseline using an exponential fit", allows both); the 5 s window is the 13 frames before the onset frame, and the subtracted variant adds back the fit's mean. These are standard choices for details the Methods do not give.

outcomes.statement: The structure of AIB's sexual dimorphism to high salt or pheromone differs between forward and backward motor states.
outcomes.source: Results, Most sensory neurons in the head exhibit sexually dimorphic responses, paragraph 11; Figure S2C
outcomes.quote: In some responses, such as AIB responding to high salt or pheromones (Figure S2C), the structure of the sexual dimorphism is different when animals are (fictively) moving forward in comparison to backward
outcomes.notes: All 48 reading combinations meet the criterion. With the mean AVA trace, fit to the whole trace and divided, (max - min) / mean, exclusion (a), AIB's high-salt onset response is dimorphic in reverse (p below 1e-4) and not in forward (p = 0.12), interaction p = 0.0027; its pheromone onset response has interaction p = 0.0012. Offset responses do not meet it.

outcomes.statement: Average responses are mostly insensitive to the animal's motor state, and many dimorphic sensory responses persist after conditioning on it.
outcomes.source: Results, Most sensory neurons in the head exhibit sexually dimorphic responses, paragraph 11; Discussion, paragraph 3; Figure S8A to S8D
outcomes.quote: Overall, however, average responses were mostly insensitive to the motor state of the animal
outcomes.notes: All 48 reading combinations meet the criterion. With the mean AVA trace, fit to the whole trace and divided, (max - min) / mean, exclusion (a), 81.7% of 672 forward against reverse comparisons over the Figure 2B to 2E classes have p > 0.05, and 37 of 48 dimorphic sensory class-cue-window responses (77%) stay dimorphic within the forward or the reverse state. Over all combinations, 77.8% to 87.2% and 69% to 82%.

outcomes.statement: Pairwise functional connectivity is highly similar between the sexes (R2 = 0.8 for a linear fit of male on hermaphrodite mean correlations).
outcomes.source: Results, Functional correlations between sex-shared neurons are predominantly shared between sexes, paragraph 2; Figure 4C
outcomes.quote: the functional connectivity between hermaphrodites and males is highly similar (80% or R2 = 0.8 for a linear fit)
outcomes.notes: Over 5995 subclass pairs, R2 = 0.806 under CORRELATION reading (b) (slope 0.871) and 0.806 under reading (a); with raw traces, R2 = 0.763.

outcomes.statement: In both sexes stimuli are more correlated or anti-correlated with sensory neurons than with interneurons or motor neurons.
outcomes.source: Results, Functional correlations between sex-shared neurons are predominantly shared between sexes, paragraph 2; Figure 4B
outcomes.quote: In both sexes, stimuli were more correlated (or anti-correlated) with sensory neurons than with interneurons ... or motor neurons
outcomes.notes: Over the 880 stimulus-subclass pairs, with the layers of Figure 3A and CORRELATION reading (b), mean |r| with sensory subclasses 0.035 in hermaphrodites and 0.036 in males, with interneurons 0.017 and 0.018, with motor neurons 0.016 and 0.015; root mean square r 0.071 and 0.075 against 0.020 to 0.026. The same under reading (a) and with the earlier assumed layers. All correlations are small.

outcomes.statement: Pharyngeal neurons show some correlations with each other but are largely uncorrelated with the rest of the brain.
outcomes.source: Results, Functional correlations between sex-shared neurons are predominantly shared between sexes, paragraph 2; Figure 4B
outcomes.quote: Neurons within the pharynx show some correlations with each other but are largely uncorrelated with the rest of the brain
outcomes.notes: CORRELATION reading (b), mean |r| of pharyngeal to non-pharyngeal pairs 0.034 in hermaphrodites and 0.038 in males, pharyngeal pairs 0.078 and 0.091, non-pharyngeal pairs 0.110 and 0.115; the same order under root mean square r and under reading (a). Pharyngeal pairs are less correlated than non-pharyngeal ones.

outcomes.statement: Almost all neuron pairs have a functional dimorphism below 0.4, on a scale of 0 to 2.
outcomes.source: Results, Functional and synaptic sexual dimorphisms are distinct, paragraph 2; Figure 4E
outcomes.quote: we observed that almost all neuronal pairs had a functional dimorphism of less than 0.4
outcomes.notes: 5994 of 5995 subclass pairs (99.98%) have a functional dimorphism below 0.4 under CORRELATION reading (b), the largest 0.414; the same under reading (a) (largest 0.411). Both readings of "almost all" (95%, 99%) hold.

outcomes.statement: The neuron names of the dandiset's traces can be matched to the cells of the four connectomes the paper compares with (White et al. 1986 as annotated by Cook et al. 2019, the male of Cook et al. 2019, and Witvliet et al. 2021 datasets 7 and 8).
outcomes.source: STAR Methods, Normalization of connectome data and Selecting neuron pairs with the highest dimorphism in synaptic and functional connectivity
outcomes.quote: Pairs not measured in the connectome data (e.g., the pharyngeal neurons and ventral nerve cord motor neurons) were also excluded
outcomes.notes: Cells are matched by name. Of the 195 recorded neuron names, 179 are in the White (Cook) matrix, 165 in the male counts matrix (185 in the male sections matrix) and 155 in each Witvliet dataset. Outside the pharynx and the ventral cord, 83 of 86 sex-shared subclasses (96.5%) have neurons in all four; AVG, SABD and SABV are not in the Witvliet datasets. All 14 pharyngeal and 10 ventral cord subclasses are missing from at least one, as the paper says; the same with Cook's counts sheets, whose White matrix (452 by 468) differs from the sections one (300 by 453). Known connections read as expected in every sheet (ASHL to AVAL 12 synapses in White's counts, 15 in its sections, 8 and 16 in Witvliet's datasets 7 and 8, none from AVAL to ASHL), which checks the parse and orientation of each sheet. White's counts give no AVAL to VA05, VA07, VA08 or VA09 synapse where its sections give 7 each; the supplements' legends say the counts hold only connections scored on electron micrographs and the sections add connections by extrapolation where no data were available. The six pairs of Figure 4F are among the most synaptically dimorphic pairs the match gives (fig4f-synaptic-top-not-functional), which supports the link.

outcomes.statement: Normalizing the three hermaphrodite connectomes by their 95% quantiles cut the mean SEM across them from 1.14 (SD 2.07) to 0.62 (SD 0.87).
outcomes.source: STAR Methods, Normalization of connectome data
outcomes.quote: This average SEM was 1.14 with a standard deviation of 2.07 ... the average SEM decreased to 0.62 (down from the initial 1.14), and the standard deviation of the SEM decreased to 0.87
outcomes.notes: Measured is reading (a), the code's set of synapses between recorded head neurons, with Cook's EM sections (2832 synapses). No reading puts all four values within tolerance. With sections over every synapse of the cells the three datasets share (reading b) the mean SEM before normalization is 1.143 (expected 1.14) but its SD 1.68 (2.07), and after normalization the mean SEM rises to 1.32 and the SD is 1.55 (expected 0.62 and 0.87). With Cook's synapse counts the values are 0.69 to 0.71 before and 0.66 after. The 95% quantiles are 22 to 25 for White's sections and 11 to 13 for the Witvliet counts, so scaling to White's quantile raises the Witvliet weights. The match of the mean SEM before normalization with sections suggests the paper used sections; the other three values still miss.
deviations: The paper's merged connectome table is not public; the four connectomes are read from the journals' supplements, and Cook's synapse counts (SI 3) and EM sections (SI 5) are both run, as the paper does not say which it used.
The 95% quantile is taken over the nonzero weights of the set; over all entries it is 0 or 1 for the larger set.

outcomes.statement: Functional and synaptic dimorphisms are uncorrelated.
outcomes.source: Results, Functional and synaptic sexual dimorphisms are distinct, paragraph 3; Figure 4D
outcomes.quote: We found no clear relationship between synaptic and functional dimorphism
outcomes.notes: Over the 3403 pairs of the 83 subclasses in all four connectomes, functional on synaptic dimorphism has slope -0.0028, R2 = 0.0001, p = 0.641 with Cook's counts, and slope -0.0005, p = 0.905 with sections; with the functional dimorphism of CORRELATION reading (a), p = 0.815 and 0.825. The code's variant (regularization 3, pairs with both sums below 3 dropped) gives p = 0.0092 with counts (400 pairs, slope -0.030, R2 = 0.017) and p = 0.085 with sections; its slope is negative.
deviations: Connectomes rebuilt from their sources, counts and sections both run (see connectome-normalization-sem). The male connectome is normalized by the same quantile rule.

outcomes.statement: The neuron pairs with the highest synaptic dimorphisms are functionally uncorrelated in both sexes and show little to no functional dimorphism.
outcomes.source: Results, Functional and synaptic sexual dimorphisms are distinct, paragraph 3; Figure 4F; Figure S4B
outcomes.quote: These pairs were functionally uncorrelated in both sexes
outcomes.notes: With counts, 35 of the top 36 pairs by synaptic dimorphism (combined SEM below 5) have no functional dimorphism under reading (a) and under (b); with sections 30 and 34. The six pairs of Figure 4F have synaptic dimorphism 0.75 to 0.88 (counts) and functional p 0.071 to 0.881, none dimorphic. Mean |r| of the six is 0.044 in hermaphrodites and 0.090 in males, and of the top 36 0.145 and 0.156 (counts); reported descriptively, as the criterion says.
deviations: Connectomes rebuilt from their sources (see connectome-normalization-sem).

outcomes.statement: The neuron pairs with the highest functional dimorphisms are mostly not synaptically connected, and where connected their connectivity is essentially not dimorphic.
outcomes.source: Results, Functional and synaptic sexual dimorphisms are distinct, paragraph 3; Figure 4G; Figure S4C
outcomes.quote: We found that these pairs were mostly not synaptically connected. When they were connected, the connectivity was essentially not dimorphic
outcomes.notes: With Cook's counts both orders of exclusion meet the criterion, (i) under both readings of not connected, 21 of 36 pairs unconnected (zero in both sexes) and 13 of 15 connected ones not dimorphic, (ii) under reading (b), 22 of 27 with both sums below 3 and 4 of 5 connected not dimorphic (11 of 27 unconnected under reading a). With Cook's sections order (i) meets it (20 of 36, 13 of 16) and order (ii) does not under either reading (10 of 27 unconnected under reading a; 21 of 27 under reading b, with 3 of 6 connected not dimorphic). The layers (Figure 3A or the earlier assumed ones), which decide the sensory-sensory exclusion of order (i), do not change these counts. With counts alone the claim would be reproduced; with sections the two orders disagree, which the criterion does not allow. The mean SEM before normalization matches the paper's 1.14 with sections (1.143) and not with counts (0.69 to 0.71), which points to sections, but neither the paper nor its code says which form or order was used. The claim is blocked because the outcome depends on that choice; the question is in the findings.
deviations: Connectomes rebuilt from their sources (see connectome-normalization-sem).

outcomes.statement: Indirect multi-hop synaptic connections are stronger between all pairs but still fail to match functional dimorphisms.
outcomes.source: Results, Functional and synaptic sexual dimorphisms are distinct, paragraph 4; Figure S20
outcomes.quote: these multi-hop indirect synaptic connections were higher between all pairs of neurons, but they failed to match the dimorphisms measured in functional connectivity
outcomes.notes: Shortest-path indirect strengths are at least the direct ones for all 3403 pairs in both sexes (median indirect hermaphrodite strength 5.85 with counts, median direct 0), and functional on indirect dimorphism has p = 0.215 with counts and p = 0.963 with sections.
deviations: Graph over the 83 subclasses present in all four connectomes, edges from the summed undirected subclass weights; connectomes rebuilt from their sources.

outcomes.statement: The stimuli evoke behavioral responses in wild-type and in the imaged NeuroPAL GCaMP6s strain, with preferences that are monomorphic for some stimuli and dimorphic for others.
outcomes.source: Results, Broad chemosensory stimulation activates the whole brain of both sexes, paragraph 1; Figure 1A and 1C; Figure S1A and S1B
outcomes.quote: These stimuli evoked robust behavioral responses in both wild-type (N2) worms and the NeuroPAL;GCaMP6s (OH16230) worms
outcomes.notes: The drop-test avoidance indices are not in the dandiset, which holds imaging only, and the paper names no other public source for them (its Data S1 to S4 are the spreadsheets behind Figures 2 to 5; its code's FigS2.ipynb reads files not in the repository).

findings.statement: Files sub-20220403-h3 (hermaphrodite) and sub-20220403-m3 (male) hold the same 382-row ActivityTraces table, with identical values and labels. It is the traces of both animals, h3's (187 rows) followed by m3's (195 rows, with the male-specific CEM and MCM neurons), as the responses show when read with each file's stimulus order. Nothing in the files says which rows belong to which animal.

The subject sex field is "O" (other) in all 47 files; the sex is given only in the subject description ("Adult hermaphrodite." or "Adult male.") and the subject id. The strain field is "[]" in every file, though the paper names strain OH16230.
The StimulusInfo timestamps are labelled seconds but hold frame numbers (up to 4980 in a 31-minute recording at 2.66 volumes/s).

The activity traces have no unit and no description beyond "list of reading at each frame". Blocks of frames are blank (the first 96 frames in 13 recordings, other ranges of 29 to 514 frames in seven) without a note of why; they are consistent with the per-recording time ranges the paper's code ignores, whose spreadsheet is not public.
The identification confidence of each neuron, which the paper's code uses to keep only confident identities, is not in the dandiset.
No tail neuron has a trace, though the paper says tail neurons were recorded and the NeuroPAL segmentations identify them. The drop-test behaviour of Figure S1 is not in the dandiset.

The stimulus annotations lie 1 to 3 frames after the fixed onset frames the paper's code uses for every recording (1323 presentations 2 frames later, 82 three and 5 one). The traces have 4979 frames, two fewer than the 4981 image volumes, and the stated rate is 2.66 volumes/s where the Methods give 2.67.
The traces cover 189 distinct sex-shared neuron names across the 47 animals, where the paper says 196 sex-shared neurons were studied.

The tracked neuron ROIs (TrackedNeuronROIs, stored identically under processing/NeuroPAL and processing/CalciumActivity, "Neuron centers as tracked throughout GCaMP video. Formatted as (x, y, z, t)") have x = y = z = 0 in 99.75% of the 44,677,593 ROIs of the 47 files; the rest, in 19 files, have no coordinate above 2, where the image volumes of the two files listed are 512 by 300 or 400 by 23 voxels. Only the fourth field varies (0 to 4980 in sub-20220327-h2). The tracked labels include tail neurons (31 with one ROI per volume in sub-20220327-h2; 284,479 ROIs in 11 files, all zero), whose traces are not in the files, so the tracked positions that would let them be extracted from the raw volumes are missing.

The connectome table the paper's code reads (prepared by S.J. Cook) is not in the repository or the dandiset, nor are neurons/neuron_classes.json, the per-recording spreadsheet of time ranges and ganglia to ignore, or the identification confidences.

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: Round 1. The executed notebook of the first run with the conclusion cells and the summary removed, the helper module and the claims file, with the paper. The verifier queried the archive's API (47 ophys NWB files), re-ran the connectome normalization from the journal supplements, and tested responses, exclude, ttest, subclass, canonical, stimulus_series and ma_past on synthetic inputs, all correct (points 4, 8, 11). Its outcomes agree with the record as it then stood for 33 of 34 claims; it gave fig2-awa-awb-nociceptive as not reproduced. Point 12 found no misreading of the paper in the claims file, so no question was added for a reader. Point 5 (the split of the shared h3 and m3 table) it judged well supported; nothing was changed. It could not check the per-stimulus counts of Figure 5B, as Data S4 is not available, nor the recorded-neuron set of the normalization; these stay unchecked. Report in transcripts/seyedolmohadesin-2026/verifier-1-report.md.

disagreements.reason: AWA is not responsive to CuSO4; smallest p = 0.077 under (a), 0.085 under (b).

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebook)
verifications.reviewed: Round 2. The full executed notebook of the revision after round 1, with its conclusions and summary, the helper module, the claims file and the attempt record, with the paper. The verifier agreed with all 34 outcomes and found no misreading of the paper in the claims file; it noted one omission, that the claims file says the layers are given only in Figure 5A and Data S4 while Figure 3A labels them, which does not change a claim's test, so no question was added for a reader. It also found that the README said the notebook spends nearly two minutes streaming the trace tables where cell 1 prints 55 s; the README now gives about one minute of about ten. Report in transcripts/seyedolmohadesin-2026/verifier-2-report.md.

paper_notes.statement: Question for the paper's authors. For the motor state from AVA (Methods, Classifying motor state), which trace is used (AVAL, AVAR or their mean), how is a change of more than 20% measured, is the exponential fitted to the whole trace or to its baseline, and is it divided or subtracted? Of the 48 combinations run here (with the two exclusion readings), 36 put the interneurons highest for Figures S3F and S3G at q < 0.05 and 12 do not, which leaves that claim blocked.

Question for the paper's authors. Which form of the Cook et al. (2019) connectomes, synapse counts or EM serial sections, went into the merged table of Figure 4, and over which values is the 95% quantile taken? The mean SEM before normalization matches the Methods' 1.14 with sections (1.143) and not with counts (0.69 to 0.71), but neither reproduces the fall to 0.62, and the Figure 4G result depends on the choice and on the order of its exclusions.

Question for the paper's authors. Which test and which neurons support "no dependence on response amplitude as a function of stimulus order" (Figure S2E)? A regression on position finds none, while a one-way ANOVA over positions finds one under the Methods' exclusion alone (p = 0.034) and not with the code's filters (p = 0.056).

entries.name: seyedolmohadesin-2026
entries.title: Whole-brain chemosensory responses of both C. elegans sexes (Seyedolmohadesin et al. 2026)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Seyedolmohadesin et al. (2026) on dandiset 000981, which holds whole-head calcium imaging of 22 hermaphrodites and 25 males during repeated presentation of ten chemosensory stimuli. It tests which neuron classes respond and which respond differently in the two sexes, examples of single classes, the dependence on motor state, and the functional connectivity of the two sexes. The connectome comparisons need published connectomes and the behavioural assays are not in the dandiset.
